name: Spruce Knob Tower Site
summary: Pendleton County, WV summit: 1916 wooden fire lookout is gone. The register says it was replaced by a stone-faced concrete observation tower; the summit tower finished in 1969 may be that replacement (not stated outright). Registered as a former lookout site in 2017.
design: Register: the 1916 wooden lookout 'has since been replaced with a stone-faced concrete observation tower'. Byrd Center: the 1969 summit observation tower has two levels of observation platforms and an enclosed space for exhibit panels. NPS: a two-story observation tower stands at the peak. The register does not date the replacement or name the 1969 tower.
status_note: The 1916 wooden fire lookout is gone. A visitor observation tower stands on the summit, finished 1969. Register and Forest Fire Lookout Association lists do not describe the observation tower as a lookout.
agency: U.S. Forest Service, Monongahela National Forest

access.note: The observation tower is found along the half-mile Whispering Spruce Trail that circles the mountain top (National Park Service). No closure found in the sources read; current conditions not checked.

visit.trail_note: Half-mile Whispering Spruce Trail circles the summit and passes the observation tower (National Park Service).

events.note: Lookout station under construction on the summit at 4,860 ft, per the 4th Biennial Report of the state Forest, Game and Fish Warden.
Moses R. Bennett put on duty as watchman in spring 1916, before the station was finished, to meet local people and distribute literature.
Summit observation tower finished in summer 1969 after work in 1966 and 1967; dedicated 13 September 1969 with a keynote by Senator Robert Byrd.
Registered 26 January 2017 as US 1641, WV 32, nominated by Brian Powell.
